name: The Sherman household — a documented dressmaker, unplaced in the town
head: sherman_h

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE PAPER, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The corpus first prints this person at the Democrat of 3 December 1834, column 21, so they are in the town's paper by 1834-12-03 and at no stated time before it; nothing reached says when they came. Last printed 1834-12-03.

lives_at.note: Not attested. NOTHING IS BEING WITHHELD HERE: no source reached says where this person lived, and 52 households in this dataset were already in that position before this one was written.

works_at.note: Not attested as a structure this project models. The trade is documented; the premises are not one of the committed records.

present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Last printed 1834-12-03, at the Democrat of 3 December 1834, column 21, and nothing reached either follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. A documented resident whose whereabouts on one day are unknown is `uncertain` here rather than dropped: that is the same distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and it is a finding rather than a gap.

persons.name: Mrs. H. Sherman

occupation.note: THE TRADE IS THE PAPER'S. The corpus reads it as dress maker, milliner, at the Democrat of 3 December 1834, column 21. The residents vocabulary's nearest period-correct word for it is `dressmaker`, and where the corpus prints more than one trade they are all named here rather than reduced to the one the vocabulary could take.

persons.note: A DOCUMENTED PERSON, AND NOTHING ELSE IS CLAIMED. The papers name ''RS. H. SHERMAN,' and give the trade; they do not say where this household lived, who else was in it, or when it came. So the record around this person carries nothing but the person: no dwelling, no division, no family, each written as unattested in its own block rather than filled in from the shape of the rest of the town. Cited at the Democrat of 3 December 1834, column 21. THE TOWN NEVER INVENTED A ROOF FOR THIS TRADE. The occupation census raised reconstructed households for the trades a town of 3,265 people needed and could not document; `dressmaker` was not one of them, which is why this person could only ever be ADDED and never seated on an existing record — data/research/newspapers/register_1835.json calls it `new_resident` for exactly that reason. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). READ THROUGH A TRANSCRIPTION, not a scan: the owner's ruling of 2026-08-28 grades a transcription-mediated reading as documented, and the source record for the run states that standard and its limits. A scan read that confirms or corrects the name upgrades this entry.

resident_research.evidence_for: Surname 'Sherman' folds to the same string as the roll line's, and the given name of both begins H.
resident_research.evidence_against: The surname 'Sherman' stands on printed pages 38-39 and no man under it carries the initial 'H' of 'Mrs. H. Sherman'. A surname-only agreement is a refusal. The surname 'Sherman' is in Norris 1844 and no entry under it carries the initial 'H' of 'Mrs. H. Sherman'. A surname-only agreement is a refusal. The surname 'Sherman' stands among the Fort Dearborn Addition bidders and no bidder under it carries the initial 'H' of 'Mrs. H. Sherman'. A surname-only agreement is a refusal. The 1835 record carries no forename at all — 'Mrs. H. Sherman' — and the volume prints Alson S., Francis Cornwell, Francis T., B. F. and N. Sherman jr. A surname-only agreement is a refusal under this project's standing rule, and an initial with no forename behind it cannot be tested against any of them.
resident_research.summary: Independently corroborated. Mrs. H. Sherman agrees, forename for forename or initial for initial, with a record outside the post-office lists in the St Cyr / St Mary registers. Surname 'Sherman' folds to the same string as the roll line's, and the given name of both begins H.
resident_research.notes: Research only. Later-volume readings are recorded here and NOT promoted: T-0513 consolidates and T-0514/T-0515 apply.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE NEWSPAPER REGISTER (T-0376), AND THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER RATHER THAN AN ARGUMENT. Every other record in this dataset argues for a household — a family the sources count, or a trade the town demonstrably needed. This one argues for a PERSON: the Democrat and the American name Mrs. H. Sherman as a dressmaker at Chicago 1 time(s), and this reconstruction did not hold them. `data/residents/` has no way to carry a person except inside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing: one member, no dwelling, no division, no origin, no arrival beyond the bound the paper sets. Reading a family, a house or a quarter of town into this record would be reading something the papers do not say. tools/mint_documented_residents.py derives the whole minted set and prints every candidate it refused, with the reason.
